setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. are Off, so offsets can land on any note of the scale. Random Note is already assigned to the first Trig params slot, and the parameter list is open for the second slot, on Twos Random Note (the manual's Random Twos Note).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Twos Random Note to the second slot and K2 to return, then turn E2 to select the first slot, Random Note. Both slots read 0. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop: the phrase is unchanged, 60, 62, 64, 65.
steps.title: Offset 0 leaves the phrase alone

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to Random Note 1: each note is its original degree or the next one up the scale. Play and stop (first pass 60, 64, 64, 65). Then turn E3 to 2: each note is its degree, one above or one below. Play and stop (first pass 59, 60, 62, 67). The MIDI strip shows this manual's fixed random run, which repeats exactly; on your norns the notes change on every pass, but always stay within the offsets named here.
steps.title: Turn Random Note up to 1, then 2

steps.caption: Turn E3 to 3: each note may move -1, 0, +1 or +2. Play and stop (first pass 60, 60, 67, 69). Then turn E3 to 4: each note may move -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees. Play and stop (first pass 57, 64, 67, 62).
steps.title: Turn Random Note up to 3, then 4

steps.caption: Turn E2 to the Twos Random Note slot, turn E3 to 4, then turn E2 back and play. The two offsets add, so each note may move anywhere from -6 to +6 scale degrees. First pass: 57, 59, 55, 64.
steps.title: Add Twos Random Note on top
